- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction, especially after sharp spikes.
- After a price spike (e.g., >45), model often overshoots in subsequent days; reduce forecast by 5–10% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-period, model fails to adjust quickly; delay or reduce upward forecast momentum until sentiment stabilizes.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion periods when sentiment is mixed or neutral; increase forecast by 2–5% for 3–7 days if recent price is above 30-day moving average.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows sharp downward trend after a positive spike, model often fails to recognize it; apply early correction if sentiment turns negative within 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is positive and price is rising, model tends to over-forecast; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent high if sentiment remains positive for >3 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misjudges turning points; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5–7 days to anchor forecast.
